author: George Kesarios
title: While Pandora ( P ) recently launched a premium on-demand st
text:
While Pandora ( P ) recently launched a premium on-demand streaming service to catch up to the competition from Apple ( AAPL ) and Spotify, it came too late in the game. 
Pandora recently unlocked on-demand free streaming, as long as the user is willing to view a 15 second video ad. Yes this was needed, but it is something that Spotify has been doing for years. Again, Pandora was late to the game.
I have been a bear on Pandora for a very long time. However, the valuation of the company has finally come down a lot, and it is something that I could finally buy. The problem is that the company is still losing money and will probably keep losing money for the foreseeable future.
The problem with Pandora can be depicted in the chart below:
P Total Operating Expenses (Quarterly) data by YCharts 
In a nutshell, no matter how high revenue grows, total operating expenses plus the cost of goods (the licensing cost of revenue) will exceed revenue, and the company will always lose money. In other words, the company is operating a loss by default. 
Please note that if this situation does not change, eventually the company will go out of business. So what has to be done? Well, the company has to increase revenue buy such an amount, so as to be able to cover operating expenses and licensing costs.
I decided to put some numbers in a spreadsheet in order to come to some conclusion as to when and if Pandora will ever be profitable. So using the company's latest historic financial results , I did some calculations (Excel sheet here ).
